dzenis-burnic.profile: A box-to-box midfielder with Dortmund academy roots, Burnić has been a consistent performer for Karlsruher SC in the 2. Bundesliga. His technical ability, pressing and ability to drive through midfield keep him relevant at international level. He is a left-footed central option who provides Bosnia with variety in their midfield configurations.
strengths: Strong technical base from BVB academy
weaknesses: Career stagnated outside top-flight football
Disciplinary record can disrupt game plans

ermin-mahmic.name: Ermin Mahmić
ermin-mahmic.profile: One of Bosnia's youngest midfielders, Mahmić spent 2024-25 at SV Lafnitz in Austria's second tier — scoring 4 goals and providing 5 assists in 25 appearances — before signing a four-year contract with Czech First League club Slovan Liberec. An attacking-minded central midfielder with excellent vision and technique, he is a rising talent whose inclusion signals Bosnia's faith in youth.
strengths: Young with significant ceiling for growth
weaknesses: Experience limited to lower European leagues
Physical development still ongoing

benjamin-tahirovic.name: Benjamin Tahirović
benjamin-tahirovic.profile: A defensive midfielder who came through Roma's academy and had a stint at Ajax before joining Brøndby on a permanent deal in February 2025. His ability to intercept, recycle possession and break up opposition attacks gives Bosnia's midfield a vital screening function. Technical quality honed at top academies makes him one of the squad's higher-potential young profiles.
strengths: Technical quality honed at top academies (Roma, Ajax)
weaknesses: Struggled for regular first-team minutes at Ajax
Scoring output from midfield is limited

amar-memic.name: Amar Memić
amar-memic.profile: A right-sided midfielder who signed for Viktoria Plzeň and featured in their UEFA Europa League campaign, Memić has developed into a reliable attacking-minded option in the Czech top flight. Capable of operating on the right flank or through the middle, he provides Bosnia with a creative midfield option with European competition experience.
strengths: Consistent contributions in Czech top flight
weaknesses: Yet to prove himself consistently in a top-five league
Final third decision-making can be inconsistent

armin-gigovic.name: Armin Gigović
armin-gigovic.profile: Gigović had a remarkable 2024-25 Bundesliga season with Holstein Kiel, scoring 5 goals in 31 league appearances — a standout return for a central midfielder in a relegated side. His energy, late runs into the box, and pressing make him one of Bosnia's most dynamic midfield options. He moved to Young Boys for 2025-26 and will use the World Cup as a springboard to a bigger move.
strengths: Strong goal-scoring output from midfield (5 Bundesliga goals)
Dynamic pressing and late runs into the box
weaknesses: Was part of a relegated Bundesliga side in 2024-25
Consistency of passing at the top level can vary

kerim-alajbegovic.name: Kerim Alajbegović
kerim-alajbegovic.profile: The most electrifying teenager in the squad, Alajbegović emerged from Bayer Leverkusen's academy and joined Salzburg for 2025-26, where he scored 7 goals in his debut season. Still only 18, he scored on his senior Bosnia debut and heads to the 2026 World Cup as one of the most exciting young wingers in Eastern Europe. His pace, dribbling, and direct running are weapons Bosnia can deploy from the bench or in wide positions.
strengths: Natural goal threat from the wing (7 goals in debut Salzburg season)
Fearless attitude at the highest level
weaknesses: Limited senior club appearances prior to Salzburg
Consistency and decision-making still raw at 18

esmir-bajraktarevic.name: Esmir Bajraktarević
esmir-bajraktarevic.profile: A MLS homegrown product who completed a $6 million move to PSV Eindhoven in January 2025, Bajraktarević won the Eredivisie title in his debut season with the Dutch giants. A pacey, left-footed right winger with sharp movement and a keen eye for goal, he is Bosnia's most exciting young attacker and his performances have already attracted Premier League interest. The 2026 World Cup could be his global breakthrough moment.
strengths: Pace and directness on the right wing
Winning mentality — Eredivisie champion in debut season
Creative and goal-threatening from wide positions
weaknesses: Minimal Eredivisie appearances in debut campaign (joined January 2025)
Physical adaptation to elite European demands ongoing

ermedin-demirovic.name: Ermedin Demirović
ermedin-demirovic.profile: Bosnia's deadliest striker and focal point of the attack, Demirović had a sensational 2024-25 Bundesliga season with 15 goals in 34 appearances, cementing his status as one of the Bundesliga's most lethal forwards. A powerful, direct centre-forward with intelligent movement and a clinical finishing instinct, he is the player opponents fear most and will be Bosnia's greatest threat at the 2026 World Cup.
strengths: Clinical finishing and elite goal-scoring instinct
weaknesses: Assist contributions are modest for a forward of his quality
Can be isolated if service is limited

jovo-lukic.name: Jovo Lukić
jovo-lukic.profile: A tall, left-footed forward who had a difficult spell at Universitatea Craiova in the first half of 2024-25 before making a career-defining move to Universitatea Cluj, where he became the Liga I top scorer in 2025-26. His physicality and aerial threat give Bosnia an alternative attacking option to Demirović, and his ability to hold up play makes him a useful squad weapon.
strengths: Aerial threat and physical presence up front
Strong link-up play as a target striker
weaknesses: Moderate goal return at Craiova in first half of 2024-25
Pace is below the elite level for a top forward

samed-bazdar.name: Samed Baždar
samed-bazdar.profile: A fast, direct winger who joined Spanish club Real Zaragoza from Partizan in July 2024, making 31 appearances and scoring 4 goals in the Segunda División, before being loaned to Jagiellonia Białystok in January 2026. Still only 21, Baždar's speed and directness give Bosnia a different attacking dimension — a runner who can exploit spaces in behind.
strengths: Ability to run in behind defensive lines
Young and improving at a high European level
weaknesses: Goal conversion rate still inconsistent
Final product (assists, goals) needs improvement

haris-tabakovic.name: Haris Tabaković
haris-tabakovic.profile: The most prolific Bosnian striker in recent domestic history, Tabaković scored 22 goals in 32 matches at Hertha BSC in 2023-24 before joining Hoffenheim for 2024-25 where he scored 6 goals in 22 appearances and was subsequently loaned to Borussia Mönchengladbach. A reliable penalty-box finisher, his intelligent movement and clinical touch make him Bosnia's most experienced domestic striker.
weaknesses: Largely a penalty-box striker with limited contribution outside the area
Age means his best World Cup is likely 2026

edin-dzeko.name: Edin Džeko
edin-dzeko.profile: The greatest Bosnian footballer of all time, Džeko joined Schalke 04 in the 2. Bundesliga as a player-mentor and showed he can still score at the top with an impressive early-season return of 6 goals in 10 appearances. With over 100 Bosnia international goals and medals from Manchester City, Roma, Inter Milan and beyond, his mere presence transforms the team's mentality. At 39, his role is as much leadership and inspiration as it is goals.
strengths: Hold-up play and link work remain elite
weaknesses: Age-related decline in pace and pressing
Cannot sustain a starting role across a full tournament

salah-zakaria.name: Salah Zakaria
salah-zakaria.profile: Salah Zakaria is Al-Duhail's first-choice goalkeeper and one of Qatar's most reliable shot-stoppers heading into 2026. A composed, technically sound keeper who commands his area well, he recorded 10 clean sheets in 22 league appearances during the 2024-25 Qatar Stars League season. At just 26, he represents the present and future of Qatari goalkeeping as the host nation plays their second-ever World Cup.
weaknesses: Limited exposure to elite European competition
Distribution under high pressure

meshaal-barsham.name: Meshaal Barsham
meshaal-barsham.profile: Meshaal Barsham is Al-Sadd's starting goalkeeper and a pivotal figure in the club's back-to-back Qatar Stars League title wins in 2023-24 and 2024-25. Named QSL Goalkeeper of the Season for 2024-25, Barsham is agile and highly capable of big saves in crucial moments. He will compete with Salah Zakaria for the starting berth at Qatar's 2026 World Cup.
weaknesses: 1.36 GA90 in rotated league appearances
Positioning on set pieces

mahmoud-abunada.name: Mahmoud Abunada
mahmoud-abunada.profile: Mahmoud Abunada is a 25-year-old goalkeeper who serves as Qatar's third-choice option heading into 2026. A tall and commanding presence at 1.91m, he plays for Al-Rayyan in the Qatar Stars League and is considered one of the country's brightest goalkeeping prospects. His inclusion in the World Cup squad reflects the depth of Qatari goalkeeping development.
strengths: Composed under pressure for his age
weaknesses: Limited senior international experience
Still developing shot-stopping consistency

boualem-khoukhi.name: Boualem Khoukhi
boualem-khoukhi.profile: Boualem Khoukhi is an Algerian-born Qatari centre-back who has been the defensive rock of both Al-Sadd and the national team for over a decade. A strong, experienced organiser at the back, he was part of Qatar's 2022 World Cup squad and brings invaluable experience to a host-nation group. Made 16 league appearances for Al-Sadd as they won the 2024-25 Qatar Stars League title.
weaknesses: Pace against fast forwards is a concern at 34
Recovery speed in transitions

pedro-miguel.name: Pedro Miguel
pedro-miguel.profile: Pedro Miguel is a Portuguese-born Qatari left back who has been one of the most consistent defenders in the Qatar Stars League for years. Renowned for his technical ability, overlapping runs, and defensive solidity, he is a key part of Al-Sadd's title-winning backline. At 34, he provides experience and versatility as Qatar seeks to progress beyond the group stage.
strengths: Technical quality and composure on the ball
Defensive positioning and reading of play
weaknesses: Pace limitations at his age against fast wingers
May struggle with elite opposition pressing high

sultan-al-brake.name: Sultan Al Brake
sultan-al-brake.profile: Sultan Al Brake is a versatile defender for Al-Duhail who can operate as a centre-back or right back, giving Qatar tactical flexibility. A Qatari international who was part of the 2022 World Cup squad on home soil, Al Brake brings domestic experience and solid defensive fundamentals to a young Qatari defensive unit.
weaknesses: Consistency levels can vary match to match
Aerial threat against taller forwards

al-hashmi-al-hussain.name: Al-Hashmi Al-Hussain
al-hashmi-al-hussain.profile: Al-Hashmi Al-Hussain is one of Qatar's most promising young defenders, having made his international debut in June 2024. The 22-year-old Al-Arabi centre-back is a tenacious tackler who is not afraid to be physical, and his elevation to the World Cup squad at this stage of his career underlines the faith placed in Qatar's next generation.
strengths: Aggressive in the tackle and strong in duels
weaknesses: Still gaining top-level experience — can be caught in possession
Disciplinary record (3 yellow, 1 red in 11 appearances)

ayoub-al-alawi.name: Ayoub Al-Alawi
ayoub-al-alawi.profile: Ayoub Al-Alawi is Qatar's youngest outfield World Cup squad member at just 20 years old. The Al-Gharafa centre-back had limited league minutes in 2024-25, making just four appearances, but his physical attributes — standing at 187cm — make him a project player that coach Lopetegui wants exposed to World Cup football. He represents Qatar's generational investment in their defensive future.
strengths: Impressive height and physicality for his age
Strong aerially and good with his feet for a centre-back
High ceiling as a developing talent
weaknesses: Very limited senior club experience in 2024-25
Tactical and positional maturity still developing

issa-laye.name: Issa Laye
issa-laye.profile: Issa Laye is a tall, commanding centre-back who joined Al-Arabi on loan in January 2025. Standing at 188cm, he is a dominant aerial presence and fits Qatar's need for physical depth at centre-back. His no-nonsense defensive approach complements more technical defenders in the squad.
strengths: Good anticipation in the defensive line
weaknesses: Only half a season of Qatar Stars League experience in 2024-25
Limited involvement at the very top of the domestic game

lucas-mendes.name: Lucas Mendes
lucas-mendes.profile: Lucas Mendes is a Brazilian-born Qatari left-sided defender who has been a cornerstone of the Qatar national team for years. Now 35, the Al-Wakrah captain brings a wealth of experience and composure under pressure. He played 15 matches for Al-Wakrah in the 2024-25 season and remains a key organiser in the backline.
strengths: Experienced leader and organiser at the back
weaknesses: Age-related decline in pace could be exposed by fast attackers
Limited impact on attacking transitions

homam-al-amin.name: Homam Al-Amin
homam-al-amin.profile: Homam Al-Amin is the only Qatar 2026 squad member playing outside of Qatar, spending the 2024-25 season on loan at Cultural Leonesa in Spain's Primera Federación (third tier). The Al-Duhail-owned left back has developed his technical game in Spanish football, giving him a level of European exposure unique in the Qatar squad.
strengths: Technically polished from Spanish football development
Athleticism and work rate up and down the flank
Positional versatility as a left back or left wing-back
weaknesses: Playing in Spain's third division — gap to World Cup level is significant
Limited international caps relative to squad peers

ahmed-fathi.name: Ahmed Fathi
ahmed-fathi.profile: Ahmed Fathi is a combative and experienced defensive midfielder who has been a mainstay of the Qatar national team. A two-time Asian Cup winner (2019 and 2023), he specialises in breaking up play, winning second balls, and providing protection to the backline. His reading of the game and work ethic make him an effective base in Qatar's midfield.
weaknesses: Limited attacking output — rarely contributes goals or assists
Disciplinary record with yellow card accumulation

jassim-gaber.name: Jassim Gaber
jassim-gaber.profile: Jassim Gaber is a 23-year-old defensive midfielder or centre-back who provides versatile cover across Qatar's back third. Born in February 2002, he is one of the youngest midfielders in the squad and his inclusion reflects Qatar's long-term planning. After featuring for Al-Rayyan during the 2024-25 season, he brings energy and mobility to the holding role.
strengths: Versatility as a midfielder and defender
weaknesses: Still relatively inexperienced at senior level
Needs to develop passing range in possession phases

assim-madibo.name: Assim Madibo
assim-madibo.profile: Assim Madibo is Qatar's first-choice central defensive midfielder and the engine of the national team's midfield. Born in Sudan and naturalised Qatari, he is the primary ball-winner who sits in front of the back four and allows Abdulaziz Hatem to operate more freely. He was a standout figure during Qatar's Asian Cup title defences.
weaknesses: Limited attack contribution — not a goal threat
Yellow card accumulation (5 in limited 2024-25 appearances)

abdulaziz-hatem.name: Abdulaziz Hatem
abdulaziz-hatem.profile: Abdulaziz Hatem is one of Qatar's most technically gifted midfielders, capable of dictating tempo and picking passes in tight spaces. Having played over 100 international caps, the Al-Rayyan veteran is the creative fulcrum of the national team's midfield alongside Madibo. Made 18 league appearances in 2024-25 and remains an important figure in Lopetegui's plans despite being 34.
weaknesses: Age-related drop in mobility and pressing output
Pace in transitions has diminished

karim-boudiaf.name: Karim Boudiaf
karim-boudiaf.profile: Karim Boudiaf is a deeply experienced box-to-box midfielder who has worn the Qatar national team shirt over 80 times. The Algerian-born Qatari international is known for his physicality, engine, and ability to contribute in both defensive and offensive phases. He was part of Qatar's 2022 World Cup squad and at 34 he provides tournament experience in the dressing room.
strengths: Experience of major tournaments including 2022 World Cup
weaknesses: Declining mobility at 34
Tendency to accumulate yellow cards

mohammed-mannai.name: Mohammed Mannai
mohammed-mannai.profile: Mohammed Mannai is the 2024-25 Qatar Stars League Best Under-23 Player of the Season, making him one of the most exciting young talents in Qatari football. On loan at Al-Shamal from Al-Sadd, the 22-year-old defensive midfielder impressed throughout the campaign with energetic performances, earning his World Cup call-up on merit.
strengths: Award-winning form at U23 level in 2024-25
Technical quality for a young defensive midfielder
weaknesses: Step up to World Cup intensity will be significant for a 22-year-old
Limited top-level experience compared to squad veterans

almoez-ali.name: Almoez Ali
almoez-ali.profile: Almoez Ali is Qatar's all-time leading scorer with 60 international goals in 126 appearances and the captain of Al-Duhail. He was the top scorer in Asia's 2026 World Cup qualifying with 12 goals, underlining his continued dominance at continental level. The Sudanese-born striker scored a record nine goals at the 2019 Asian Cup and is Qatar's most potent attacking threat entering 2026.
strengths: Elite finishing and movement in the box
Ability to lead the line physically and technically
weaknesses: Effectiveness can depend on service quality from midfield
Inconsistency in club form across seasons

akram-afif.name: Akram Afif
akram-afif.profile: Akram Afif is Qatar's most celebrated footballer and a two-time AFC Player of the Year. The Al-Sadd left winger finished as joint-top scorer in the 2024-25 Qatar Stars League with 18 goals, driving Al-Sadd to back-to-back league titles. Afif has 127 international caps and 40 goals for Qatar, with his hat-trick of penalties in the 2024 Asian Cup final cementing his legendary status. He is the undisputed leader of Qatar's attack for 2026.
strengths: Dribbling ability and unpredictability in the final third
Unmatched big-game mentality — decisive in Asian Cup finals
weaknesses: Heavily relied upon — Qatar's attack can be one-dimensional without him
Physical intensity of World Cup tournament football over multiple games

tahsin-mohammed.name: Tahsin Mohammed
tahsin-mohammed.profile: Tahsin Mohammed is Qatar's most exciting teenage talent, born June 16, 2006, and one of the youngest players at the 2026 World Cup. The Al-Duhail winger is quick, direct, and blessed with natural technical ability. His inclusion in the 26-man squad at just 19 demonstrates the ambition of Qatar's footballing programme to fast-track gifted young players onto the world stage.
strengths: Electrifying pace and directness on the wing
Natural technical talent with outstanding potential
weaknesses: Very young and inexperienced at professional level
Consistency and decision-making still developing

edmilson-junior.name: Edmilson Junior
edmilson-junior.profile: Edmilson Junior is a Brazilian-born Qatari international winger who plays on the right flank for Al-Duhail. A dynamic and technically skilled wide forward, he provides direct running, crosses, and goal threat from the right side, complementing Akram Afif on the other flank. His naturalisation for Qatar adds significant quality to the national team's wide attacking options.
strengths: Dynamic direct running and dribbling from the right
Technical quality and ability to create chances
weaknesses: Consistency of end product can fluctuate
Defensive tracking back is sometimes lacking

ahmed-al-janehi.name: Ahmed Al-Janehi
ahmed-al-janehi.profile: Ahmed Al-Janehi is a 24-year-old attacking midfielder or wide forward who had an impressive 2024-25 campaign for Al-Gharafa, registering 3 goals and 6 assists in the Qatar Stars League. His ability to operate between the lines and create for teammates as well as score gives Qatar a versatile option across the front line.
strengths: Creative vision and assist ability — 6 QSL assists in 2024-25
weaknesses: Still developing his goal-scoring output
Can be inconsistent against physically dominant defenders

ahmed-alaa.name: Ahmed Alaa
ahmed-alaa.profile: Ahmed Alaa is a 32-year-old forward for Al-Rayyan who has been a consistent performer in the Qatar Stars League over many years. Known for his movement, link-up play, and eye for goal, he provides experienced attacking options for Qatar from the bench or wide positions. A reliable domestic campaigner, he brings consistency and experience to complement the squad's younger attackers.
strengths: Consistent performer across multiple QSL seasons
Ability to operate across front line positions
weaknesses: Not an elite goal scorer by international standards
Pace may limit effectiveness against top-level defences

hassan-al-haydos.name: Hassan Al-Haydos
hassan-al-haydos.profile: Hassan Al-Haydos is Qatar's captain and most-capped player ever, with 188 international appearances and 41 goals. He came out of international retirement in June 2025 at the personal request of head coach Julen Lopetegui. A creative wide forward known for his dribbling, vision, and ability to perform in the biggest moments, Al-Haydos symbolises Qatari football.
strengths: Dribbling, vision, and quality in the final third
Leadership and motivational presence as captain
weaknesses: At 35, sustained high-intensity runs are limited
Physical output has declined from peak years

mohammed-muntari.name: Mohammed Muntari
mohammed-muntari.profile: Mohammed Muntari made history at the 2022 World Cup by scoring Qatar's only goal of the tournament — a memorable header against Senegal. Having joined Al-Gharafa on a free transfer in summer 2024, he scored 4 goals in 10 league appearances in his debut season. The 27-year-old provides a different physical profile up front compared to Almoez Ali, and his World Cup goal-scoring pedigree makes him a meaningful option.
weaknesses: Limited appearances in 2024-25 — still settling at new club
Not the most prolific scorer at club level

yusuf-abdurisag.name: Yusuf Abdurisag
yusuf-abdurisag.profile: Yusuf Abdurisag is a 24-year-old winger who spent the 2024-25 season on loan at Al-Wakrah from parent club Al-Sadd. A pacey and energetic wide forward, he is one of Qatar's most dynamic young attackers with the ability to run in behind defences and create problems on the counter. His development loan at Al-Wakrah has given him valuable regular game time ahead of his first World Cup.
strengths: Pace and direct running in behind defences
Young age with high developmental ceiling
Ability to play across the front line
weaknesses: End product needs improvement — goals and assists not yet elite
Experience of high-pressure knockout football limited

marvin-keller.name: Marvin Keller
marvin-keller.profile: Marvin Keller is the long-serving Young Boys goalkeeper who has been the undisputed first choice in Bern for several seasons. A calm and technically sound shot-stopper, he earned his place as Switzerland's third-choice keeper through consistent Swiss Super League performances and UEFA Champions League experience. At the 2026 World Cup he serves as experienced domestic cover behind Kobel.
weaknesses: Limited top-level European exposure
Tested by high-volume shot opponents

gregor-kobel.name: Gregor Kobel
gregor-kobel.profile: Gregor Kobel is Switzerland's undisputed number one and one of the top goalkeepers in the Bundesliga. After helping Dortmund reach the 2024 Champions League final and delivering another commanding season in 2024-25, Kobel arrives at the 2026 World Cup as one of the most reliable and dominant keepers in the tournament. His aerial presence, composure under pressure, and sweeping ability make him the cornerstone of Switzerland's compact defensive system.
weaknesses: Can be prone to distribution errors under intense pressure
Has not consistently reproduced peak UCL-level form in all Bundesliga matches

yvon-mvogo.name: Yvon Mvogo
yvon-mvogo.profile: Yvon Mvogo had arguably his best professional season in 2024-25, helping Lorient win the Ligue 2 title and earn promotion back to Ligue 1. A solid and experienced shot-stopper who has played across multiple European leagues, Mvogo provides reliable competition for the second-choice goalkeeper slot behind Kobel heading into the 2026 World Cup.
weaknesses: Limited top-flight exposure in recent seasons
Aerial command can be uncertain against physical strikers

manuel-akanji.name: Manuel Akanji
manuel-akanji.profile: Manuel Akanji is Switzerland's most accomplished center-back, joining Inter Milan on loan from Manchester City in 2024-25 and becoming a key figure in Simone Inzaghi's title-challenging side with 33 Serie A appearances. His ball-playing ability, aerial presence, and positional intelligence make him the defensive leader of the Swiss national team. He will be pivotal in marshalling Switzerland's back line through the knockout stages of the 2026 World Cup.
weaknesses: Can be exposed by quick transitions against top pace
Occasionally rash in the challenge

aurele-amenda.name: Aurèle Amenda
aurele-amenda.profile: Aurèle Amenda is one of Switzerland's most exciting young defenders who moved to Eintracht Frankfurt in 2024 and earned limited but impactful Bundesliga minutes in his debut season (~200 minutes). A commanding center-back with excellent anticipation, strong dueling ability, and poise on the ball, Amenda represents the future of the Swiss defensive setup.
strengths: Strong in aerial and ground duels
Composure on the ball for his age
weaknesses: Limited Bundesliga minutes in 2024-25 (200 total)
Still building experience against top-level forwards

eray-comert.name: Eray Cömert
eray-comert.profile: Eray Cömert is a composed and technically capable center-back who has established himself in La Liga with Valencia. His 2024-25 season was disrupted by a hamstring injury that limited him to 16 La Liga appearances, but he combines solid defensive fundamentals with the technical quality prized in the Swiss national team and remains an important depth option.
weaknesses: Injury susceptibility has limited availability
Aerial duels against elite strikers can be challenging

nico-elvedi.name: Nico Elvedi
nico-elvedi.profile: Nico Elvedi is a dependable and experienced center-back who has been a fixture for both Switzerland and Borussia Mönchengladbach for nearly a decade. Leading his club with 174 clearances in the 2024-25 Bundesliga, he has been a cornerstone of Switzerland's defensive solidity across multiple World Cups and European Championships. He brings calm leadership to the defensive unit.
strengths: High clearance volume and defensive organisation (174 in 2024-25)
Experience and consistency at the highest domestic level
weaknesses: Pace against quick forwards in behind
Ball progression from the back is functional rather than creative

luca-jaques.name: Luca Jäques
luca-jaques.profile: Luca Jäques is a promising young Swiss center-back who joined VfB Stuttgart on a permanent deal in February 2025 and quickly made an impression, capping his debut season by winning the DFB Pokal. A modern ball-playing defender who is composed under pressure and strong in one-on-one situations, Jäques is one of the most exciting young Swiss defenders heading into the World Cup.
weaknesses: Still building Bundesliga experience with limited minutes in 2024-25
Tested by physical elite strikers at top-level

miro-muheim.name: Miro Muheim
miro-muheim.profile: Miro Muheim is a versatile and energetic left-back who has been a consistent performer for Hamburger SV, making 30 2. Bundesliga appearances in 2024-25. Known for his overlapping runs, defensive intensity, and ability to contribute to attacks from wide areas, Muheim has become a reliable option on the left flank for Switzerland.
strengths: Overlapping runs and attacking contribution from left-back
weaknesses: Crossing can be inconsistent under pressure
Transition defending when caught high up the pitch

ricardo-rodriguez.name: Ricardo Rodríguez
ricardo-rodriguez.profile: Ricardo Rodríguez is one of Switzerland's most experienced defenders, a veteran left-back who joined Real Betis on a free transfer in August 2024 after leaving Torino, making 18 La Liga appearances in 2024-25. Renowned for his delivery from set-pieces and dependable defensive performances, Rodríguez has been a fixture in Swiss squads for over a decade.
weaknesses: Reduced pace at 32 against young attacking wingers
Limited to a depth role given squad age profile

silvan-widmer.name: Silvan Widmer
silvan-widmer.profile: Silvan Widmer is an experienced and versatile right-back who has served Switzerland well across multiple major tournaments. In 2024-25, his role at Mainz 05 shifted to a squad rotation option with only 3 starts across 27 Bundesliga appearances. His ability to play both full-back positions and deliver from set-pieces makes him valuable experienced depth for Switzerland.
weaknesses: Reduced to a rotational role at club level in 2024-25
Pace limitations against younger wingers

michel-aebischer.name: Michel Aebischer
michel-aebischer.profile: Michel Aebischer is a dynamic box-to-box midfielder who moved on loan from Bologna to Pisa for the 2024-25 Serie A season after years of consistent performances at Bologna during their historic Champions League qualification. A key figure in Switzerland's midfield for several years, he combines pressing intensity, ball recovery, and intelligent forward carrying.
weaknesses: Pisa loan limited his profile compared to earlier Bologna seasons
Pass completion can drop under sustained high pressure

remo-freuler.name: Remo Freuler
remo-freuler.profile: Remo Freuler is one of Switzerland's most experienced and respected midfielders, a mainstay of the national team for nearly a decade. At Bologna in 2024-25, he made 28 Serie A appearances, recording 81 tackles across the season while contributing his trademark combination of elite pressing, defensive interceptions, and quality distribution. At 33, this may be his final World Cup.
strengths: Elite work rate and tackling volume across a full season
Experience as a tournament veteran for Switzerland
weaknesses: Aging legs may limit back-to-back high-intensity performances
Declining vertical passing range compared to peak years

ardon-jashari.name: Ardon Jashari
ardon-jashari.profile: Ardon Jashari was the breakout star of the 2024-25 Belgian Pro League season at Club Brugge, earning both Player of the Year and Young Player of the Year honours after a dominant campaign. A dynamic defensive and progressive midfielder with exceptional ball retention, dribbling under pressure, and line-breaking passing ability, his move to AC Milan in summer 2025 cemented his status as one of Europe's most exciting young midfield talents.
strengths: Ball retention and dribbling under pressure
Defensive intensity and one-on-one ball recovery
weaknesses: Yet to be tested consistently at Serie A level after summer 2025 move
Can overcommit in pressing situations

fabian-rieder.name: Fabian Rieder
fabian-rieder.profile: Fabian Rieder is a versatile and technically gifted attacking midfielder who spent the 2024-25 season on loan at VfB Stuttgart from Stade Rennais, contributing 8 assists and 1 goal in 21 Bundesliga appearances and winning the DFB Pokal. A player with an excellent eye for the through-ball and solid pressing intelligence, Rieder subsequently made a permanent move to FC Augsburg.
strengths: Versatility across midfield and attacking positions
weaknesses: Inconsistency in high-pressure moments
Defensive contribution still developing at the highest level

djibril-sow.name: Djibril Sow
djibril-sow.profile: Djibril Sow is a powerful and progressive defensive midfielder who has established himself as a key player at Sevilla after his move from Eintracht Frankfurt. With a 90% pass completion rate and strong defensive metrics across 30 La Liga appearances in 2024-25, Sow provides both disciplined protection and quality ball circulation. He is the athletic engine in the Swiss midfield.
strengths: High pass completion rate (90% in La Liga)
weaknesses: Goal contribution from midfield remains modest
Can occasionally overdo risky carries into pressure

granit-xhaka.name: Granit Xhaka
granit-xhaka.profile: Granit Xhaka is the heartbeat of the Swiss national team and one of the most transformed midfielders in European football. His 2024-25 season with Bayer Leverkusen — where he led the Bundesliga in line-breaking passes (550) and helped win the domestic double — was arguably the peak of his career renaissance. Now captaining Sunderland in the Premier League, Xhaka brings unparalleled leadership, vision, and passing range to Switzerland.
strengths: Elite line-breaking passing range — led Bundesliga in 2024-25
High defensive duel contribution and coverage
weaknesses: Occasional disciplinary issues under sustained pressure
Reduced burst of pace at 33

denis-zakaria.name: Denis Zakaria
denis-zakaria.profile: Denis Zakaria enjoyed one of the best seasons of his career at Monaco in 2024-25, scoring 6 goals and providing 5 assists from central midfield while helping Monaco qualify for the Champions League. Setting personal career bests in goals, assists, and tackles with 33 appearances, Zakaria re-established himself as a top-level player after years of injury disruption.
strengths: Powerful surging runs from deep midfield
Goal and assist contribution from central areas
weaknesses: Injury history has disrupted consistency throughout his career
Can be tactically undisciplined when pressing aggressively

ruben-vargas.name: Ruben Vargas
ruben-vargas.profile: Ruben Vargas is a versatile and direct winger who split the 2024-25 season between FC Augsburg in the Bundesliga (August–January) and Sevilla in La Liga after a January 2025 transfer. Known for his direct running, intelligent movement off the ball, and ability to cut inside, Vargas is a key creative and attacking threat on the left flank for Switzerland.
strengths: Contributes in both attack and pressing phases
weaknesses: End product in front of goal can be inconsistent
Winter transfer disrupted early-season rhythm at Augsburg

zeki-amdouni.name: Zeki Amdouni
zeki-amdouni.profile: Zeki Amdouni spent the 2024-25 season on loan at Benfica in the Primeira Liga, where he scored 5 goals in 18 appearances while developing his game in a top Portuguese club environment. A powerful and intelligent centre-forward with excellent link-up play and movement in behind defensive lines, Amdouni is one of Switzerland's most technically rounded attackers.
strengths: Physical presence and hold-up play in attack
weaknesses: Shot accuracy at Benfica was below expectations (7 on target from 29 shots)
Adapting between different club environments has disrupted rhythm

breel-embolo.name: Breel Embolo
breel-embolo.profile: Breel Embolo had his finest season in years at Monaco in 2024-25, scoring 7 goals and providing 7 assists in 39 appearances — setting career highs across multiple attacking and defensive metrics. The powerful and versatile forward combines exceptional physicality with sharp pressing intelligence and clever movement. Now at Rennes, Embolo remains Switzerland's most complete and experienced attacking option entering the 2026 World Cup.
strengths: Goal and assist contributions from varied positions
weaknesses: Injury proneness has been a recurring concern throughout his career
Can go quiet in matches when service from midfield is limited

dan-ndoye.name: Dan Ndoye
dan-ndoye.profile: Dan Ndoye had a breakthrough 2024-25 Serie A season at Bologna, scoring 8 goals and providing 4 assists in 30 appearances, including the winning goal in the Coppa Italia final — Bologna's first major trophy in over 50 years. An electric winger whose ball-carrying statistics were bettered by only five players in all of Serie A, his versatility, pace, and ability to perform in big matches make him one of the most dangerous wide players at the 2026 World Cup.
strengths: Electric ball-carrying and dribbling — Serie A top 5
Versatility across both wings and attacking positions
Proven big-game delivery at the highest level
weaknesses: Shot accuracy on high volume can be inconsistent
Decision-making in the final third under sustained defensive pressure

noah-okafor.name: Noah Okafor
noah-okafor.profile: Noah Okafor had a difficult 2024-25 season, making only 11 Serie A appearances for AC Milan before a planned RB Leipzig loan fell through following a failed medical, then moving on loan to Napoli in February 2025 where he contributed sparingly but won the Scudetto. A player of exceptional pace, technical quality, and positional versatility, he remains one of the highest-ceiling players in the Swiss squad. His move to Leeds for 2025-26 provides a new platform.
weaknesses: Club inconsistency throughout 2024-25 limited form and confidence
Final ball and penalty area decision-making need sharpening

christian-fassnacht.name: Christian Fassnacht
christian-fassnacht.profile: Christian Fassnacht returned to Young Boys in January 2025 after a stint at Norwich City, and immediately reverted to the prolific form that made him one of the Swiss Super League's most feared forwards, scoring 11 goals in just 18 league appearances in the second half of the season. His clinical instinct, intelligent movement, and technical ability remain fully intact at 31.
strengths: Clinical finishing at Swiss Super League level (11 goals in 18 apps)
Experience and leadership as a senior forward in the squad
weaknesses: Period at Norwich City saw limited minutes and disrupted form
Pace naturally declining with age at 31

cedric-itten.name: Cédric Itten
cedric-itten.profile: Cédric Itten is a powerful and direct centre-forward who had a productive 2024-25 season at Young Boys, scoring 8 goals in 34 Swiss Super League appearances before earning a move to Fortuna Düsseldorf in the 2. Bundesliga. A traditional number nine with physical strength, aerial presence, and an ability to hold up play, Itten provides a different attacking profile to the other Swiss forwards.
strengths: Physical hold-up play and link-up with runners
Aerial threat from crosses and set-pieces
Work rate and pressing from the front line
weaknesses: Swiss Super League background limits exposure to elite-level defenders
Finishing can be streaky over a full season

johan-manzambi.name: Johan Manzambi
johan-manzambi.profile: Johan Manzambi is one of the most exciting young Swiss forwards to emerge in recent seasons, breaking onto the Bundesliga scene at SC Freiburg in the second half of 2024-25 with 2 goals and an assist across six successive appearances. A quick, direct, and technically gifted winger, his form earned him his first senior Switzerland call-ups and a place in the 2026 World Cup squad at just 22.
strengths: Explosive direct running and dribbling at pace
Hunger and confidence of a young talent with rising trajectory
weaknesses: Very limited top-flight Bundesliga experience (11 appearances in 2024-25)
Decision-making under defensive pressure still developing

alisson.name: Alisson
alisson.profile: Alisson is widely regarded as one of the finest goalkeepers of his generation, combining elite shot-stopping with commanding presence and distribution that allows Liverpool to play out from the back. He won the Premier League Golden Glove for 2024-25, recording 9 clean sheets in 28 appearances despite missing several matches through injury. At the 2026 World Cup, he provides Brazil with an immovable presence between the posts and a leader of the defensive unit.
strengths: Distribution and ability to initiate attacks
Leadership and command of the penalty area
weaknesses: Injury vulnerability reduced appearances in 2024-25
Occasionally overconfident in coming off his line

ederson.name: Ederson
ederson.profile: Ederson built his reputation at Manchester City as a sweeper-keeper with exceptional with-the-ball ability, revolutionising the goalkeeper position under Pep Guardiola. His 2024-25 season was his worst at City, keeping just 10 clean sheets in 26 Premier League appearances as the team struggled collectively, leading to his summer 2025 move to Fenerbahce. He brings experience and composure as Brazil's second-choice goalkeeper at the 2026 World Cup.
weaknesses: Save percentage declined in a poor 2024-25 City season
Questions about form after difficult final campaign at City

weverton.name: Weverton
weverton.profile: Weverton is a veteran Brazilian goalkeeper who spent a decade as the undisputed number one at Palmeiras, winning two Copa Libertadores titles before joining Gremio in early 2026. During the 2024 Brasileirao season at Palmeiras, he was among the league's most reliable stoppers with a 79.5% save rate and 16 clean sheets in 37 appearances. At the 2026 World Cup, he serves as Brazil's experienced third-choice option.
strengths: Proven reliability in high-stakes Brasileirao matches
Shot-stopping consistency over a long career
weaknesses: Age (38) limits athleticism compared to younger alternatives
Less exposure to elite European football

wesley.name: Wesley
wesley.profile: Wesley is a dynamic right-back who became one of the most coveted young defenders in South America during his time at Flamengo, earning a €30 million move to Roma in the summer of 2025. In the 2024 Brasileirao he made 31 appearances from right-back, contributing 2 assists and impressing with his athleticism in one-on-one duels. At 21, he is one of Brazil's most exciting defensive prospects for the 2026 World Cup with the pace and ability to threaten from wide positions.
strengths: Exceptional athleticism and speed in 1v1 duels
Strong aerial ability for his age
weaknesses: Still developing defensive positioning at the highest level
Limited top-level European experience before the tournament

douglas-santos.name: Douglas Santos
douglas-santos.profile: Douglas Santos is a reliable left-back who has spent several years with Zenit St. Petersburg in the Russian Premier League, providing steady defensive cover and occasional attacking threat from wide areas. In 2024-25 he made 30 league appearances and contributed 1 goal, maintaining consistency in a high-level domestic environment. He offers Brazil experienced back-up at left-back for the 2026 World Cup.
weaknesses: Playing in the Russian Premier League limits exposure to top-level competition
Lack of high-profile recent form against elite opponents

alex-sandro.name: Alex Sandro
alex-sandro.profile: Alex Sandro is a veteran left-back who returned to Brazil with Flamengo in August 2024 after a decade in European football with Juventus. In 26 appearances in 2025 (covering the 2024-25 period), he demonstrated continued quality with 49 clearances, 24 tackles, and a 72% aerial duel success rate. His inclusion in Brazil's 2026 World Cup squad reflects his leadership qualities and the experience he brings to the defensive unit, even at 34.
strengths: Elite aerial dueling (72% win rate) for a full-back
High pass accuracy (89%) in build-up play
Defensive experience from Juventus and Serie A
weaknesses: Age limits pace and recovery against quick wingers
No longer the attacking force he was at his peak

gabriel-magalhaes.name: Gabriel Magalhaes
gabriel-magalhaes.profile: Gabriel Magalhaes has established himself as one of the Premier League's most dominant centre-backs, combining aerial authority with an aggressive pressing game that suits Arsenal's high-defensive-line system. In 2024-25 he made 28 league appearances, won 79 aerial duels, made 89 clearances, scored 3 goals, and kept 17 clean sheets. He is Brazil's first-choice centre-back at the 2026 World Cup and one of their most important defensive pillars.
strengths: Dominant in the air (79 aerial duels won in 2024-25)
Goals from set pieces add a genuine threat (3 in 2024-25)
weaknesses: Can be drawn out of position when overcommitting to challenges
Suspension risk due to aggressive style

marquinhos.name: Marquinhos
marquinhos.profile: Marquinhos is Brazil's long-standing defensive captain, a technically refined centre-back who has led PSG and his national team with authority throughout the past decade. In a 2024-25 Ligue 1 season disrupted by injury and rotation, he made 19 appearances and scored 2 goals, maintaining his quality when available. For the 2026 World Cup he brings irreplaceable leadership and organisational intelligence to Brazil's defence.
strengths: Elite positional intelligence and reading of the game
Ability to play as a defensive midfielder if needed
weaknesses: Limited to 19 Ligue 1 appearances in 2024-25 due to PSG rotation
Has struggled to recapture his very best form in recent seasons

danilo.name: Danilo
danilo.profile: Danilo is a versatile experienced defender who spent five years at Juventus before joining Flamengo on a free transfer in January 2025. He can play right-back, centre-back, or as a defensive midfielder, making him a key utility option. In 26 appearances post-joining Flamengo (covering the 2024-25 period), he scored 5 goals and provided tactical leadership. He is Brazil's defensive captain at the 2026 World Cup with unmatched experience from Real Madrid, Manchester City, and Juventus.
strengths: Positional versatility across the entire backline
Elite reading of the game from years at top clubs
weaknesses: Age (34) means reduced dynamism in full-back roles
Transition from top European football to Brasileirao took adjustment

bremer.name: Bremer
bremer.profile: Bremer was arguably Juventus' best player in the opening weeks of 2024-25, playing every minute of the first 8 appearances and recording 6 interceptions and 11 blocks before suffering a torn ACL against RB Leipzig in October 2024, ending his season. He returned fully fit for the 2025-26 season, and his inclusion in Brazil's 2026 World Cup squad reflects his immense talent — a physically commanding defender who combines elite athleticism with technical quality.
strengths: Exceptional physical attributes and aerial dominance
Dominant in the air and on the ground before injury
weaknesses: Returning from ACL surgery with limited competitive minutes since October 2024
Risk of rust after prolonged absence at the World Cup

ibanez.name: Ibanez
ibanez.profile: Roger Ibanez is a rugged, aggressive centre-back who joined Al-Ahli from Roma for €30 million in 2023 and has remained a consistent presence in the Saudi Pro League. He won the AFC Champions League Elite in 2024-25 with Al-Ahli and maintained regular appearances in a competitive environment. At the 2026 World Cup he provides depth at centre-back with his combative style and experience in European and now Saudi football.
strengths: Experience in top European and Middle Eastern football
weaknesses: Can be rash and prone to yellow cards (disciplinary record)
Playing in Saudi Pro League limits top-level competitive testing

leo-pereira.name: Leo Pereira
leo-pereira.profile: Leo Pereira is a commanding centre-back who has established himself as one of the most consistent defenders in Brazilian football, appearing in 63 matches across all competitions in 2025 for Flamengo. In the 2024 Brasileirao he played 30 league games and was integral to Flamengo's defensive structure with a 92% pass completion rate in build-up play. His form earned him a first Brazil call-up and makes him a significant defensive option for the 2026 World Cup.
strengths: Outstanding pass completion rate (92%) for a centre-back
Consistent high-volume appearances across all competitions
weaknesses: Limited previous international experience before 2026
Occasionally slow to press aggressively in tight spaces

bruno-guimaraes.name: Bruno Guimaraes
bruno-guimaraes.profile: Bruno Guimaraes is one of the Premier League's elite midfielders, combining relentless pressing, exceptional ball recovery, and underrated goal threat from deep positions. In 2024-25 he was an iron man for Newcastle, appearing in all 38 league matches with 5 goals and 6 assists while covering more distance than any other Premier League player (263 miles). He is Brazil's undisputed midfield engine for the 2026 World Cup, capable of dominating matches both with and without the ball.
strengths: Unmatched work rate and distance covered in the Premier League
Goals and assists from midfield (11 direct contributions in 2024-25)
weaknesses: Can receive excessive yellow cards (7 in 2024-25)
Occasional overaggression leads to fouls in dangerous areas

casemiro.name: Casemiro
casemiro.profile: Casemiro remains one of the most decorated defensive midfielders in football history, a five-time Champions League winner at Real Madrid, though his 2024-25 campaign at Manchester United was difficult: he managed 24 appearances averaging just 62 minutes per game as United endured one of their worst modern seasons. His form dipped alongside the team but he retains the positional intelligence and winning mentality that make him a key figure in Brazil's World Cup midfield setup.
strengths: World-class positional reading and defensive screening
Winning experience at the highest level
Leadership and tactical intelligence built over 15 years
weaknesses: Declined physically in 2024-25 at Manchester United
Reduced playing time and form at club level questioned his peak level

danilo-santos.name: Danilo Santos
danilo-santos.profile: Danilo Santos is a young defensive midfielder who suffered a serious ankle injury on the opening day of the 2024-25 season at Nottingham Forest (Bournemouth, August 2024), missing most of the campaign before returning in January 2025 for around 12 appearances. He was subsequently released and joined Botafogo in July 2025. Strong in the tackle and adept at breaking up play, he offers Brazil a combative midfield option for the 2026 World Cup.
strengths: Strong ball-winning ability in central areas
Physical presence and discipline in midfield
Adaptability shown by moving clubs effectively
weaknesses: Limited 2024-25 appearances due to serious ankle injury
Unproven at the very highest international level

fabinho.name: Fabinho
fabinho.profile: Fabinho was one of the world's best defensive midfielders during his Liverpool years but has continued to evolve at Al-Ittihad in Saudi Arabia, winning the Saudi Pro League in 2024-25. He made 32 appearances in the Saudi Pro League, contributing 2 goals and 1 assist while receiving 8 yellow cards that reflect his combative style. At 31, he remains a quality screener in front of the Brazil backline and brings Champions League and World Cup experience to the 2026 squad.
strengths: Experience winning trophies at the highest level (Champions League 2019)
weaknesses: Saudi Pro League level not comparable to top European competitions
Accumulated 8 yellow cards in 2024-25 suggesting disciplinary risk

lucas-paqueta.name: Lucas Paqueta
lucas-paqueta.profile: Lucas Paqueta is a technically gifted attacking midfielder who thrives in the number 8 or 10 role, combining creative passing with direct dribbling and an eye for goal. After three seasons at West Ham, he returned to Flamengo in January 2026 for €42 million following the resolution of his FA betting investigation. In 2024-25 he made approximately 22 Premier League appearances for West Ham with 4 goals and 5 assists before his mid-season departure. He is central to Brazil's creative plans at the 2026 World Cup.
strengths: Exceptional technical quality and creative vision
Ability to connect defence and attack in tight spaces
weaknesses: Inconsistency at club level with West Ham's poor 2024-25 campaign
FA investigation created prolonged off-field distraction

raphinha.name: Raphinha
raphinha.profile: Raphinha produced one of the most extraordinary individual seasons in recent European football in 2024-25, scoring 18 goals and 9 assists in 36 La Liga appearances as Barcelona won the domestic treble. Named the best player in La Liga, his 43 shots on target was a personal record and his performances put him firmly in the Ballon d'Or conversation. For Brazil at the 2026 World Cup he is their most in-form attacking threat and provides world-class quality from wide areas.
strengths: Elite goal and assist output (27 combined in La Liga 2024-25)
Named La Liga's best player in 2024-25
Versatility to play wide or centrally in attacking positions
weaknesses: Must sustain that peak level after an extraordinary 2024-25
Has historically been inconsistent for Brazil compared to club form

neymar.name: Neymar
neymar.profile: Neymar returned to Santos in January 2025 after terminating his contract with Al-Hilal, seeking to recover form and fitness ahead of the 2026 World Cup on home soil. He made approximately 21 appearances in the 2025 Brasileirao season, scoring 6 goals and 3 assists as he worked his way back from a long ACL injury. A former world number one, his inclusion reflects his immense talent and the significance of the tournament but his fitness and form remain question marks.
strengths: Generational technical ability and dribbling skill
Experience and leadership in high-pressure international tournaments
weaknesses: Prolonged injury history (ACL) severely reduced minutes and sharpness
Not at his previous elite level following years of injuries and Al-Hilal spell

vinicius-junior.name: Vinicius Junior
vinicius-junior.profile: Vinicius Junior is one of the most electrifying forwards in world football, combining devastating pace with improved finishing and creative vision. In 2024-25 he scored 11 goals and 8 assists in 30 La Liga appearances, taking a career-high 81 shots while also suffering more fouls than almost any other player in Europe. Brazil's talisman and most dangerous attacking weapon, he is the player every opponent at the 2026 World Cup will plan around first.
strengths: Career-high 81 shots in 2024-25 La Liga showing improved consistency
Champions League pedigree and big-game experience
weaknesses: Shots on target conversion could be higher (28/81 shots on target)
Subject to intense fouling and can lose composure under provocation

luiz-henrique.name: Luiz Henrique
luiz-henrique.profile: Luiz Henrique is a pacey, direct winger who has developed steadily since joining Zenit St. Petersburg, becoming one of the Russian Premier League's most dangerous forwards. In 2024-25 he made 28 league appearances, scoring 6 goals and 3 assists with 17 shots on target from 51 total attempts. He provides Brazil with a wide option combining speed, directness and developing creativity at the 2026 World Cup.
strengths: Raw pace and directness in wide areas
weaknesses: Limited to Russian Premier League exposure reduces credibility of stats against elite opponents
Shot accuracy (17/51 = 33%) suggests wastefulness in front of goal

matheus-cunha.name: Matheus Cunha
matheus-cunha.profile: Matheus Cunha was the standout performer for Wolverhampton Wanderers in 2024-25, scoring a career-best 15 Premier League goals with 6 assists in 33 appearances as their leading scorer, earning a £60 million move to Manchester United in August 2025. His combination of clinical finishing, link-up play, and ability to press from the front makes him one of Brazil's most versatile attacking options for the 2026 World Cup.
strengths: Versatility to play across the frontline
High pressing and work rate alongside goal threat
weaknesses: Adapting to a new club (Manchester United) just before the tournament
Consistency can vary in high-pressure big matches

gabriel-martinelli.name: Gabriel Martinelli
gabriel-martinelli.profile: Gabriel Martinelli is an explosive left winger whose energy, pressing, and direct running make him one of Arsenal's most important attacking outlets. In 2024-25 he scored 8 goals and 4 assists in 33 Premier League appearances, also scoring the winner against Real Madrid at the Bernabeu in the Champions League quarter-finals. His pace and pressing from the front are invaluable for Brazil's high-intensity style at the 2026 World Cup.
strengths: Relentless pressing and energy from wide positions
Champions League experience including goals against elite opposition
Directness and ability to create chances from nothing
weaknesses: Goal output (8) below his potential given his quality
Injury history has interrupted key periods in previous seasons

igor-thiago.name: Igor Thiago
igor-thiago.profile: Igor Thiago had an extremely difficult debut season at Brentford in 2024-25, suffering a pre-season meniscus injury that kept him out until November, before a joint infection then ended his season again, limiting him to just 8 Premier League appearances with no goals. He returned to full fitness for 2025-26 and became one of the Premier League's top scorers, setting a record for a Brazilian striker. His inclusion reflects his 2025-26 form rather than a strong 2024-25 showing.
strengths: Proven Premier League goal-scoring ability (breakout in 2025-26)
Physical presence as a striker combined with technical quality
Represents the future of Brazilian strikers in European football
weaknesses: Extremely limited 2024-25 appearances (8) due to injuries
No goals in his 2024-25 Premier League season

endrick.name: Endrick
endrick.profile: Endrick is one of the most exciting teenage forwards in world football, joining Real Madrid from Palmeiras in a €60 million deal in the summer of 2024. In his debut La Liga season he made 22 appearances but was limited to just 351 minutes (largely as a substitute), scoring 1 goal - though he became the youngest foreigner to score for Real Madrid in La Liga history. His extraordinary talent was evident in Brazil's national team, and the 2026 World Cup provides a stage for this generational talent to announce himself globally.
strengths: Exceptional natural finishing instinct beyond his years
Explosive acceleration and directness in small spaces
Mental composure in front of goal for a teenager
weaknesses: Very limited Real Madrid minutes in 2024-25 (351 total) — not yet a starter
Consistency over a full 90 minutes still being developed

rayan.name: Rayan
rayan.profile: Rayan is a teenage winger who made 33 appearances for Vasco da Gama in the 2024 Brasileirao, scoring 2 goals, before earning a high-profile move to Bournemouth in January 2026. He scored on his Premier League home debut against Aston Villa and made an immediate impression in English football. At 19, he is one of Brazil's most exciting young wide forwards and the 2026 World Cup on home soil represents a potential star-making moment for the teenager.
strengths: Exceptional pace and directness from wide positions
Immediate Premier League impact on arrival at Bournemouth
Fearless and technically gifted for his age
weaknesses: Very limited top-level international experience
Still adapting to Premier League and European football intensity

yassine-bounou.name: Yassine Bounou
yassine-bounou.profile: Known as 'Bono', Bounou is Morocco's undisputed first-choice goalkeeper and one of the best shot-stoppers of his generation. His acrobatic saves and commanding presence anchored Morocco's historic 2022 semi-final run and he remains the heartbeat of their backline. At 33, he enters the 2026 World Cup as a deeply experienced leader on home territory.
weaknesses: Distribution under pressure can be erratic
Age beginning to affect consistency in high-volume seasons

munir-el-kajoui.name: Munir El Kajoui
munir-el-kajoui.profile: Munir is a vastly experienced goalkeeper who has bounced between European and African football across a long career. Joining RS Berkane in 2024, he was instrumental in their historic Botola Pro title and CAF Confederation Cup double. He serves as reliable competition for Bounou and brings continental experience to the squad.
weaknesses: Limited top-flight European experience in recent years
Unlikely to displace Bounou

ahmed-reda-tagnaouti.name: Ahmed Reda Tagnaouti
ahmed-reda-tagnaouti.profile: Tagnaouti is a senior international keeper who has been in Morocco's squads for several years. He spent the second half of 2024-25 at Moghreb Tetouan in the Botola Pro after joining them in January 2025, before moving to AS FAR in the summer of 2025. He provides dependable domestic depth behind Bounou.
weaknesses: Limited exposure to elite European football
Third-choice status limits World Cup impact

noussair-mazraoui.name: Noussair Mazraoui
noussair-mazraoui.profile: Mazraoui was one of Manchester United's standout performers in a turbulent 2024-25 season, ranking fifth in the entire Premier League for tackles won and first for tackling dribblers. His versatility — deployed at right-back, left-back, centre-back, and even as an attacking midfielder — made him indispensable. He is a key right-sided option for Morocco heading into a home World Cup.
strengths: High work rate and pressing intensity
weaknesses: Can be caught out of position when attacking
Inconsistent delivery from wide areas

anass-salah-eddine.name: Anass Salah-Eddine
anass-salah-eddine.profile: Salah-Eddine spent the first half of 2024-25 at FC Twente in the Eredivisie before a €8 million move to AS Roma in February 2025, highlighting his rapid rise. A dynamic left-back with a strong attacking bent, he contributes goals and assists from deep. He represents Morocco's next generation of full-backs and is among the younger, hungrier players in the 2026 squad.
strengths: Composure in possession at international level
weaknesses: Can be exposed defensively one-on-one
Still building top-level European consistency

youssef-belammari.name: Youssef Belammari
youssef-belammari.profile: Belammari is a left-back playing for Egyptian giants Al-Ahly, where he has developed into a reliable and attack-minded defender. His performances in the Egyptian Premier League and CAF Champions League have earned him a Morocco call-up. He offers a left-back option with energy and threat going forward, and is one of the more intriguing inclusions in the 2026 squad.
weaknesses: Unproven at top European level
Aerial defensiveness is a relative weakness

nayef-aguerd.name: Nayef Aguerd
nayef-aguerd.profile: Aguerd spent 2024-25 on loan at Real Sociedad after leaving West Ham, rediscovering his best form and earning the nickname 'Nayef Airlines' for his aerial dominance. He led Real Sociedad in clearances with 37 and maintained a 70% aerial duel success rate. Now at Marseille, he is Morocco's most complete centre-back and a vital organiser for the Atlas Lions.
strengths: Dominant in aerial duels (70%+ win rate)
Excellent reading of play and positioning
weaknesses: Injury history disrupted previous seasons
Can be vulnerable to pacey forwards in behind

chadi-riad.name: Chadi Riad
chadi-riad.profile: Riad is one of Morocco's most promising young centre-backs, signed by Crystal Palace for £14 million in 2024. His 2024-25 debut season was tragically disrupted by two separate knee injuries that limited him to just three appearances. Fully recovered, the 2026 World Cup on home soil represents a massive opportunity for the talented ball-playing defender.
strengths: Technical quality on the ball for a centre-back
High ceiling as a young player at a Premier League club
weaknesses: Injury fragility is a major concern
Very limited competitive game time in 2024-25

issa-diop.name: Issa Diop
issa-diop.profile: Diop is a powerful, imposing centre-back who has been a regular Premier League starter at Fulham. Though French-born, he committed to Morocco internationally. In 2024-25 he made 21 Premier League appearances, contributing 75 clearances and winning 19 aerial duels. His physical presence and experience in England's top flight give Morocco an imposing option at the back.
strengths: Commanding aerial presence and physical power
weaknesses: Not always convincing when playing out from the back
Pace limitations against elite forwards

redouane-halhal.name: Redouane Halhal
redouane-halhal.profile: Halhal signed for Mechelen in August 2024 and was loaned to Helmond Sport in the Dutch Eerste Divisie for 2024-25. The young full-back gained valuable first-team experience in the Netherlands, developing his defensive fundamentals. He is a long-term investment for Morocco and his 2026 inclusion reflects the national team's faith in his potential.
strengths: Young age and high development trajectory
weaknesses: Lack of top-flight senior experience
Still raw defensively under sustained pressure

achraf-hakimi.name: Achraf Hakimi
achraf-hakimi.profile: Hakimi is Morocco's talisman and arguably the best right-back in the world. His 2024-25 Ligue 1 campaign was exceptional — 4 goals and 6 assists in 25 matches — combining elite defensive work (1.9 tackles/game) with devastating attacking output. Captaining Morocco at a home World Cup, Hakimi carries enormous expectations and the quality to deliver.
strengths: Elite dribbling and progressive carrying ability
Consistent defensive contribution with 1.9 tackles per game
weaknesses: Occasionally drawn too high up the pitch, leaving space behind
Can lose composure in very high-pressure moments

zakaria-el-ouahdi.name: Zakaria El Ouahdi
zakaria-el-ouahdi.profile: El Ouahdi had a superb 2024-25 campaign for Genk in the Belgian First Division A, making 35 appearances and scoring 6 goals from right-back — an outstanding attacking return for a defender. His forward-thinking style and technical quality have made him a genuine contender for Morocco's right flank at the 2026 World Cup.
strengths: Exceptional attacking output for a defender (6 goals)
Ball-carrying and progressive passing from right-back
weaknesses: Belgian top flight may not fully prepare him for World Cup intensity
Defensive positioning can be caught when committing forward

samir-el-mourabet.name: Samir El Mourabet
samir-el-mourabet.profile: El Mourabet is one of the most exciting young midfielders to emerge from the Moroccan pool, playing as a defensive midfielder for Strasbourg in Ligue 1. At just 20 he has established himself as a regular starter, showing combativeness and composure in possession beyond his years. His inclusion in the 2026 squad reflects Morocco's rich midfield depth.
strengths: Intelligent positioning for a young defensive midfielder
Strong passing accuracy in tight spaces
weaknesses: Limited Champions League or elite European experience
Physical maturity still developing

ayyoub-bouaddi.name: Ayyoub Bouaddi
ayyoub-bouaddi.profile: Bouaddi is a generational talent — he played his first Champions League start on his 17th birthday, starting for Lille against Real Madrid on October 2, 2024. A combative, forward-thinking midfielder with elite duel-winning ability, he was one of the youngest players to feature regularly in Ligue 1 in 2024-25. His selection for the 2026 World Cup, still only 17, is among the most extraordinary stories in Moroccan football.
strengths: Exceptional maturity and composure for his age
Elite dueling intensity, ranking among Ligue 1's most active
Quick vertical passing and ability to win the ball
weaknesses: Age and physical development remains a limiting factor
Still accumulating top-level experience

neil-el-aynaoui.name: Neil El Aynaoui
neil-el-aynaoui.profile: El Aynaoui made 19 Serie A appearances for Roma in 2024-25, steadily building a reputation as a dynamic box-to-box midfielder with excellent ball interception ability. French-born with Moroccan heritage, he chose the Atlas Lions and brings a technically polished, high-energy profile to the midfield. He is expected to play an increasing role as Morocco seeks to replicate their 2022 heroics.
strengths: Strong ball-winning instincts rated 'Very Strong' by analysts
Good technical quality in tight Serie A spaces
weaknesses: Goal threat from midfield is limited
Still inconsistent as a regular starter at Roma

sofyan-amrabat.name: Sofyan Amrabat
sofyan-amrabat.profile: Amrabat was the breakout star of Morocco's stunning 2022 World Cup run, becoming a global icon as a tenacious, dominant defensive midfielder. In 2024-25 he was on loan at Fenerbahce in Turkey's Super Lig, where he made 26 appearances, occasionally completing 111 touches and 91 passes in a single match. Now at Real Betis, he remains Morocco's defensive midfield anchor.
strengths: World Cup pedigree and mental fortitude in big moments
weaknesses: Goal and creativity output from midfield is minimal
Can pick up yellow cards accumulating fouls

azzedine-ounahi.name: Azzedine Ounahi
azzedine-ounahi.profile: Ounahi burst onto the global scene at the 2022 World Cup with dynamic, energetic performances in Morocco's midfield. In 2024-25 he was loaned to Panathinaikos in the Greek Super League, scoring 6 goals and contributing 2 assists in 19 appearances while rediscovering his best form. Now signed permanently by Girona, he enters the 2026 World Cup full of confidence.
strengths: Dynamic box-to-box energy and goal-scoring threat from midfield
Strong dribbling ability and forward runs
Big-match temperament forged at 2022 World Cup
weaknesses: Can be inconsistent in defensive duties
Has struggled for continuity since his 2022 peak

bilal-el-khannous.name: Bilal El Khannous
bilal-el-khannous.profile: El Khannous was one of Leicester City's few bright spots in their relegation season of 2024-25, making 30 Premier League appearances and registering 2 goals and 3 assists. Born in Belgium, he brings European polish and a modern, progressive midfield profile. Now at Stuttgart in the Bundesliga, he is among Morocco's most technically gifted young midfielders.
strengths: Technical quality and passing range in tight spaces
Creative vision and ability to progress play
Emerged with credit from a relegation battle at Leicester
weaknesses: Defensive contribution can be limited
Physical robustness is still developing

ismael-saibari.name: Ismaël Saibari
ismael-saibari.profile: Saibari was sensational for PSV in 2024-25, recording 11 goals and 11 assists in 29 Eredivisie matches as part of their title-winning campaign, and 15 goals and 13 assists across all competitions. An attacking midfielder with elite technical ability and goal-scoring instincts, he represents Morocco's most dangerous goal threat from midfield. He is a crucial weapon for the Atlas Lions at the 2026 World Cup.
strengths: Elite goals and assists return (11G/11A in Eredivisie)
Ability to unlock defences with quick combinations
weaknesses: Eredivisie level may not fully translate to World Cup intensity
Defensive work rate can be inconsistent

abde-ezzalzouli.name: Abde Ezzalzouli
abde-ezzalzouli.profile: Known as 'Ez Abde', Ezzalzouli is a direct, pacey winger who made 32 La Liga appearances for Real Betis in 2024-25. He had a quieter statistical season (2G, 2A) but was a consistent threat with his dribbling and running in behind defences as Betis reached a historic European final. He adds width and direct running to Morocco's attacking options.
strengths: Consistent starter in La Liga at a European-level club
Provides direct threat in behind defences
weaknesses: End product — goals and assists — was limited in 2024-25
Can be wasteful when shooting opportunities arise

chemsdine-talbi.name: Chemsdine Talbi
chemsdine-talbi.profile: Talbi is a electrifying Belgian-born Moroccan winger who had a breakthrough 2024-25 season at Club Brugge, scoring 5 league goals in 27 appearances and netting a famous Champions League brace against Atalanta. Now at Sunderland in the Premier League, his technical flair and pace make him one of Morocco's most exciting young attackers heading into the 2026 World Cup.
strengths: Champions League quality dribbling and direct running
Clinical finishing when one-on-one with the keeper
Young, fearless mentality on the big stage
weaknesses: Still developing consistency across a full season
Decision-making under pressure can let him down

soufiane-rahimi.name: Soufiane Rahimi
soufiane-rahimi.profile: Rahimi is a prolific goalscorer who has thrived in the UAE Pro League with Al-Ain, becoming the club's most decisive foreign player in history. In 2024-25 he scored 9 goals in 16 UAE Pro League appearances despite missing time, and also contributed in the AFC Champions League. His pace and clinical instinct in the box make him a genuine goalscoring threat for Morocco.
strengths: Natural goalscoring instinct and clinical finishing
Pace to stretch defences in behind
weaknesses: UAE Pro League pedigree is significantly below World Cup level
Unproven against elite international defences

ayoub-el-kaabi.name: Ayoub El Kaabi
ayoub-el-kaabi.profile: El Kaabi was the finest striker in Greek football in 2024-25, scoring 18 Super League goals in 28 appearances and 7 Europa League goals in 8 games to fire Olympiacos to the title. He is a complete centre-forward — powerful, technically strong, and lethal in front of goal with 45 shots on target in the league alone. He goes into the 2026 World Cup in the form of his career.
strengths: Elite goal-scoring output (18 Super League goals + 7 Europa League goals)
Consistency and big-game mentality in European competition
weaknesses: Playing in a less competitive league than peers
Movement outside the box and link-up play is secondary to direct goal threat

brahim-diaz.name: Brahim Díaz
brahim-diaz.profile: Spanish-born but committed to Morocco, Brahim Díaz is a technically brilliant attacking midfielder/winger who operates in Real Madrid's squad. In 2024-25 he made 29 La Liga appearances with 1 goal and 6 assists, largely from the bench at the world's biggest club. His technical quality and experience at Real Madrid adds a special dimension to Morocco's attack, and a home World Cup could be his defining stage.
strengths: Elite technical ability honed at Real Madrid
Creative dribbling and assist-making in tight spaces
Experience in the highest-pressure Champions League environments
weaknesses: Limited as a starter at Real Madrid, reducing minutes and rhythm
Goal output (1 La Liga goal) was modest in 2024-25

yassine-gessim.name: Yassine Gessim
yassine-gessim.profile: Gessim is a rapid, direct right-winger who spent 2024-25 at USL Dunkerque in Ligue 2, where he established himself as a player of the month candidate. He signed for Strasbourg in January 2026 and immediately impressed in Ligue 1. His electric pace and direct play earned a Morocco call-up, and the 2026 World Cup represents an extraordinary leap for a player who was in France's second tier a year earlier.
strengths: Explosive pace and direct dribbling ability
Creative output in tight Ligue 2 situations
Fearless mentality and willingness to take on defenders
weaknesses: Very limited top-flight experience before 2026
End product and decision-making at higher levels still unproven

ayoube-amaimouni.name: Ayoube Amaimouni
ayoube-amaimouni.profile: Amaimouni is an explosive young winger who spent 2024-25 tearing apart the Regionalliga with Hoffenheim II, scoring 7 goals and 9 assists in 18 matches to fire the side to the fourth-tier title. His form attracted Eintracht Frankfurt, who signed him in January 2026. Moroccan heritage gives him international eligibility, and his selection is a bold one for the 2026 World Cup.
strengths: Blistering pace and direct running on the flank
Exceptional goals and assists output at youth level (7G/9A)
Hunger and raw potential as an emerging talent
weaknesses: No senior top-flight Bundesliga experience before 2026
Significant step-up from Regionalliga to World Cup football

johnny-placide.name: Johnny Placide
johnny-placide.profile: A veteran shot-stopper and one of the most experienced Haitian goalkeepers ever, Placide serves as a reassuring elder presence and back-up option in the squad. His decades of professional experience across France's top divisions bring invaluable organizational calm to Haiti's historic first World Cup campaign.
weaknesses: Age limits explosiveness
Limited recent top-flight exposure

alexandre-pierre.name: Alexandre Pierre
alexandre-pierre.profile: The heir apparent between the posts for Haiti, Pierre emerged as the undisputed starter in qualification and is considered the nation's goalkeeper of the future. Trained in the French system, he combines athletic reflexes with composed distribution, and his performances for the national team were pivotal in securing historic World Cup qualification.
weaknesses: Limited experience at the very top level
Inconsistent commanding crosses

josue-duverger.name: Josue Duverger
josue-duverger.profile: Playing at Rheinlandliga level in Germany's amateur pyramid, Duverger is a third-choice keeper who symbolises Haiti's depth challenge ahead of the 2026 World Cup. His inclusion in the squad reflects the federation's belief in his potential and desire to expose players to the World Cup environment.
strengths: Athletic frame for a young keeper
weaknesses: Plays in Germany's amateur sixth tier
Minimal professional track record

carlens-arcus.name: Carlens Arcus
carlens-arcus.profile: A dominant centre-back who made an immediate impact after joining Angers from Vitesse, Arcus was one of the most reliable defenders in Ligue 1 in 2024-25. Physically imposing with excellent aerial ability, he is Haiti's defensive cornerstone and brings top-flight Ligue 1 experience into the World Cup.
weaknesses: Late-season injury concerns affected availability
Can be drawn out of position when pressing

wilguens-paugain.name: Wilguens Paugain
wilguens-paugain.profile: A versatile right-back who split 2024-25 between Austrian club St. Pölten and a loan at Belgian side Zulte Waregem, Paugain brings pace and directness to Haiti's flank. His ability to get forward and cross provides an additional attacking dimension for a team that will need every creative outlet at the World Cup.
strengths: Pace and athleticism down the flank
weaknesses: Can be exposed defending 1v1 at pace
Consistency across different leagues needed

duke-lacroix.name: Duke Lacroix
duke-lacroix.profile: A veteran fullback and one of the fastest and most versatile defenders in the USL Championship, Lacroix has been a stalwart for both club and country. In the 2025 USL season he delivered consistent defensive performances and clutch assists, earning team-of-the-week recognition. His experience and athleticism are key for Haiti's World Cup backline.
weaknesses: Plays in USL Championship (3rd tier)
Age may limit endurance against elite competition

martin-experience.name: Martin Experience
martin-experience.profile: A dependable left-back who covered every minute available in France's Championnat National for Nancy, Experience brings reliability and positional intelligence to Haiti's squad. His reading of the game allows him to break up attacks early and contribute to build-up, making him a steady option in the squad.
weaknesses: Limited attacking output
Plays in France's third tier

jean-kevin-duverne.name: Jean-Kévin Duverne
jean-kevin-duverne.profile: A dependable centre-back who has established himself in the Belgian Pro League with KAA Gent, Duverne is one of Haiti's most technically refined defenders. Comfortable in a high defensive line and strong in the air, he adds solidity and composure to the backline ahead of Haiti's maiden World Cup showing.
weaknesses: Limited top European competition appearances
Can be susceptible to quick transitions

ricardo-ade.name: Ricardo Adé
ricardo-ade.profile: One of the most experienced players in the squad, Adé is an elder statesman of Haitian football who has plied his trade in Ecuador for years.
