Despite his age he remained a regular starter for LDU Quito across 30 matches in 2024-25, offering experience and leadership that will be vital in the World Cup dressing room.
strengths: Reading the game to cut out danger
weaknesses: Age limits explosive pace
Vulnerability against fast wide forwards

hannes-delcroix.name: Hannes Delcroix
hannes-delcroix.profile: A left-footed centre-back with pace and technical quality developed through Belgian football, Delcroix had a solid loan spell at Swansea in the Championship before joining Lugano in January 2026. His ability to defend high up the pitch and carry the ball makes him a modern defensive asset for Haiti's World Cup campaign.
strengths: Pace to defend a high line
weaknesses: Injury history disrupted continuity
Adapting to a new club late in the season

keeto-thermoncy.name: Keeto Thermoncy
keeto-thermoncy.profile: At just 20 years old, Thermoncy is one of the youngest players in Haiti's World Cup squad and represents the next generation of Haitian footballers developed in Switzerland. His inclusion in the 26-man roster for the tournament is a statement of faith from the coaching staff in his long-term potential.
weaknesses: Very inexperienced at senior level
Plays in Swiss Promotion League (3rd tier)

leverton-pierre.name: Leverton Pierre
leverton-pierre.profile: A combative defensive midfielder with experience across multiple levels of French football, Pierre spent 2024-25 at Châteauroux in the Championnat National before earning a move to FC Vizela in Portugal. His work rate, ball-winning ability and passing range make him a reliable engine room option for Haiti.
weaknesses: Bookings accumulation (7 yellows in 2024-25)
Can lack composure in tight spaces

carl-fred-sainthe.name: Carl-Fred Sainthe
carl-fred-sainthe.profile: One of the most statistically impressive midfielders in the 2025 USL Championship season, Sainthe posted a 90.9% pass completion rate across 28 appearances for Phoenix Rising before joining El Paso. An FC Dallas academy product with a brilliant footballing mind, he represents a key developmental talent for Haiti's midfield going into the World Cup.
strengths: High ball recovery and interception volume
weaknesses: Plays in USL Championship (3rd tier)
Yet to test himself consistently at a higher level

danley-jean-jacques.name: Danley Jean Jacques
danley-jean-jacques.profile: Arguably Haiti's best defensive midfielder and one of the top holding midfielders in MLS, Jean Jacques made 34 appearances for Philadelphia Union in 2025 including 3 goals. His intelligence, tenacity and positional discipline form the foundation of Haiti's midfield press, and he enters the World Cup as one of the squad's most valuable players.
strengths: Composure in possession for a defensive midfielder
weaknesses: Knee injury concern heading into the tournament
Can be overly conservative when Union need creativity

jean-ricner-bellegarde.name: Jean-Ricner Bellegarde
jean-ricner-bellegarde.profile: Haiti's undisputed star and the jewel of their World Cup squad, Bellegarde registered 2 goals and 7 assists in 35 Premier League appearances for Wolves in 2024-25 — a career-high 9 goal contributions. An engine-box midfielder with remarkable ball-recovery instincts and incisive passing, he is the most technically complete player in Haitian football history and the focal point of the nation's ambitions at the 2026 World Cup.
strengths: Premier League-tested ball recovery and work rate
Elite chance creation and progressive passing
Reads the game to make crucial interceptions
weaknesses: Defensive discipline in 1v1 situations can be exploited
Long-distance shooting relies on volume over precision

woodensky-pierre.name: Woodensky Pierre
woodensky-pierre.profile: A remarkable teenage talent who won back-to-back Haitian league titles with Violette AC and was named MVP of both the regular season and the finals in 2026, Pierre is the only squad member who lives and plays in Haiti. His inclusion is both symbolically powerful and a genuine footballing statement — he is an elite performer at domestic level and will represent his people in the most literal sense.
strengths: Outstanding vision and final third passing
weaknesses: No professional exposure outside Haiti
Large quality gap from Haitian Division 1 to international level

dominique-simon.name: Dominique Simon
dominique-simon.profile: A PSG and Aubervilliers academy product now establishing himself in Central European football, Simon brings technical quality and footballing intelligence to Haiti's midfield options. After 16 appearances for Pardubice in the Czech First League in 2024-25, he joined Tatran Prešov on loan. His passing pedigree and defensive recovery make him a useful squad midfielder.
strengths: Technical quality developed in top French academies
Good press resistance in tight spaces
weaknesses: Has yet to fully establish himself at one club
Limited physical presence for a central midfielder

louicius-deedson.name: Louicius Deedson
louicius-deedson.profile: An extremely productive winger in the Danish Superliga, Deedson had one of his best seasons in 2024-25 with 7 goals and 7 assists in 29 appearances for Odense, earning a move to FC Dallas. His direct running, explosive acceleration and eye for goal make him a genuine threat from wide positions and one of Haiti's most dangerous wide attackers at the World Cup.
strengths: Relentless work rate in both directions
weaknesses: Yet to prove himself in MLS
Can lack consistency in the final decision

ruben-providence.name: Ruben Providence
ruben-providence.profile: An AS Roma academy graduate who has worked through Austrian and Dutch football to establish himself at Almere City, Providence is a tricky wide forward whose movement and technique stand out. He struggled for goals in his debut Eerste Divisie season but his ability to create chances and international record of 5 goals in 20 caps demonstrates his quality.
weaknesses: Only 0 goals in 22 Eerste Divisie appearances in 2024-25
Needs to convert ability into consistent club-level output

josue-casimir.name: Josue Casimir
josue-casimir.profile: A versatile winger who scored 4 goals in 27 Ligue 1 appearances for Le Havre in 2024-25 before earning a move to Auxerre, Casimir brings top-flight French football experience to Haiti's attack. Comfortable on either wing and capable of both dribbling past defenders and cutting inside to shoot, he offers creative unpredictability at the World Cup.
strengths: Ability to operate on both flanks
weaknesses: End product (goals/assists) can be inconsistent
Has yet to fully nail down a regular starting role

derrick-etienne-jr.name: Derrick Etienne Jr.
derrick-etienne-jr.profile: A seasoned MLS winger with years of experience at New York Red Bulls and now Toronto FC, Etienne brings pace, craft and tactical discipline to Haiti's attacking options. While 2025 was a quieter personal season with reduced starts, his World Cup experience (he played for Haiti in 2022 qualifying) and ability to unlock spaces with direct running make him a dangerous impact option.
weaknesses: Goals contribution down in 2025 season
Getting into his late twenties with dip in form

wilson-isidor.name: Wilson Isidor
wilson-isidor.profile: The most feared forward in Haiti's arsenal, Isidor was Sunderland's top scorer with 13 goals in 46 appearances in the 2024-25 Championship, firing the club to play-off final victory and promotion to the Premier League. Powerful, fast, and technically accomplished, he spearheads Haiti's attack at the World Cup and will be the player opponents fear most. His €18.5m market value reflects his status as a top European forward.
strengths: Exceptional physical attributes — pace, power, aerial threat
Clinical finishing with right foot and body
weaknesses: All 13 Championship goals were non-headers — aerial conversion rate in box needs improvement
Will face Premier League standard defenders at the World Cup for first time

duckens-nazon.name: Duckens Nazon
duckens-nazon.profile: A proven striker and one of Haiti's most reliable goal-scorers, Nazon spent 2024-25 at Kayserispor in Turkey's Süper Lig where he scored 8 goals in 33 appearances, before securing a three-year deal at Esteghlal in Iran. His physical presence, finishing ability and experience across European leagues provide Haiti with a hard-working, combative number 9 option.
strengths: Proven goalscorer across multiple European leagues
Work rate and pressing from the front
weaknesses: Declining pace at 32
Has moved toward lower-prestige leagues in recent seasons

frantzdy-pierrot.name: Frantzdy Pierrot
frantzdy-pierrot.profile: A tall, powerful centre-forward who scored 6 goals in 28 appearances for AEK Athens in the Greek Super League in 2024-25, Pierrot uses his 194cm frame to dominant defenders in the air and as a focal point in the press. His hold-up play and flick-on ability give Haiti a completely different attacking dimension, and his experience at this level provides seasoned leadership.
weaknesses: Pace is not a strength at this level
On loan at Rizespor suggesting reduced status at parent club

yassin-fortune.name: Yassin Fortune
yassin-fortune.profile: An Arsenal academy graduate who has built his career through Swiss and French football, Fortune spent 2024-25 at Quevilly Rouen in the French National scoring 5 goals in 28 appearances before joining FC Vizela in Portugal. His technical quality, quick feet and versatility across the forward line offer Haiti a skillful attacking option.
strengths: Technical dribbling developed at Arsenal academy
Versatile forward — can play wide or through the middle
weaknesses: Has yet to establish himself consistently above the third tier
Goal threat needs to be more sustained

lenny-joseph.name: Lenny Joseph
lenny-joseph.profile: A powerful, direct centre-forward who scored 6 goals across Ligue 2 and Hungarian NB I in 2024-25, Joseph hit the ground running after his January 2025 move to Ferencváros, netting 4 times in 10 appearances. Playing for one of Eastern Europe's biggest clubs — who compete in European football — he brings genuine top-level ambition and a strong physical presence to Haiti's World Cup attack.
strengths: Strong in the air and physically imposing
Goal instinct in box (4 in 10 for Ferencváros)
weaknesses: Still building international experience
Arriving late at Ferencváros means he is still adapting

craig-gordon.name: Craig Gordon
craig-gordon.profile: A veteran Scottish goalkeeper who has served as Scotland's number one for over a decade. Gordon made 33 Premiership appearances for Hearts in 2024-25 despite the club's turbulent campaign. At 42, he remains Scotland's most experienced keeper heading into the nation's first World Cup since 1998, bringing calm leadership under pressure.
weaknesses: Age-related decline in mobility
Poor save percentage in 2024-25

angus-gunn.name: Angus Gunn
angus-gunn.profile: Son of former Scotland international Bryan Gunn, Angus had a solid 2024-25 season as Norwich City's first-choice goalkeeper in the Championship before joining Nottingham Forest in August 2025. His shot-stopping reliability and composure in one-on-one situations make him a reliable backup option for Scotland at the World Cup.
weaknesses: Limited top-flight experience
Aerial command under pressure from crosses

liam-kelly.name: Liam Kelly
liam-kelly.profile: A composed, technically sound goalkeeper who joined Rangers and played as deputy to the club's first choice in 2024-25, making 10 Premiership appearances and keeping four clean sheets. Kelly brings reliable shot-stopping and is Scotland's third-choice keeper, providing experienced cover at the World Cup.
weaknesses: Limited regular starts in 2024-25
Unproven at top level over extended runs

grant-hanley.name: Grant Hanley
grant-hanley.profile: A rugged, commanding centre-back who captained Scotland before John McGinn. After leaving Norwich City in January 2025 he joined Birmingham City and helped them win League One. Now at Hibernian in the Scottish Premiership, Hanley brings veteran experience and leadership to Scotland's defence at what is likely his final major tournament.
weaknesses: Reduced pace at 34
Inconsistent performances at Norwich in 2024-25

jack-hendry.name: Jack Hendry
jack-hendry.profile: A composed ball-playing centre-back who has reinvented his career in the Saudi Pro League with Al-Ettifaq. He made 15 appearances in 2024-25 after missing time through injury and suspension. Comfortable in possession, Hendry gives Scotland an option to build from the back and has been a consistent international performer.
weaknesses: Injury-interrupted 2024-25 campaign
Disciplinary record (red card in 2024-25)

aaron-hickey.name: Aaron Hickey
aaron-hickey.profile: A dynamic attacking full-back who suffered a serious hamstring injury in October 2023 that ruled him out for nearly two full seasons. He returned to fitness in 2025 and was recalled to the Scotland squad just in time for the World Cup. His direct, attacking style from left-back adds a different dimension and at 23, the tournament could relaunch his career at the highest level.
weaknesses: Long injury absence affecting match sharpness
Minimal 2024-25 competitive minutes

dominic-hyam.name: Dominic Hyam
dominic-hyam.profile: A dependable, no-nonsense centre-back who played every minute of Blackburn Rovers' 2024-25 Championship season, demonstrating exactly the kind of consistency that earns international recognition. Now at Wrexham after their rise through the divisions, Hyam provides solidity and reliability in the middle of Scotland's back four.
weaknesses: Limited in terms of playing out from the back
Not tested at Premier League level

scott-mckenna.name: Scott McKenna
scott-mckenna.profile: A powerful, physical centre-back who moved to Las Palmas in La Liga in 2024-25 before joining Dinamo Zagreb. At Las Palmas he made 27 league appearances and established himself as one of their defensive pillars with 57 clearances in his last nine starts alone. Won the Croatian league and cup double in his first season at Zagreb, arriving at the World Cup in excellent form.
weaknesses: Disciplinary record (6 yellow cards, 1 red in La Liga 2024-25)
Can be caught in behind by quick forwards

nathan-patterson.name: Nathan Patterson
nathan-patterson.profile: A rapid, energetic right-back whose career has been consistently disrupted by injuries. Patterson made just 10 Premier League appearances for Everton in 2024-25 due to foot and groin problems. When fit, he is Scotland's first-choice right-back thanks to his athleticism and dynamic overlapping runs. The World Cup represents a chance to show his quality at the highest level.
weaknesses: Persistent injury issues
Limited 2024-25 minutes (347 in PL)

anthony-ralston.name: Anthony Ralston
anthony-ralston.profile: A reliable, technically adept right-back who has been an integral part of Celtic's dominant Scottish Premiership teams. In 2024-25 he won another league title with Celtic, contributing 2 goals and 3 assists in his 8 starts. Ralston offers Scotland a domestically excellent option at right-back and brings winning mentality from Celtic's sustained success.
strengths: Technical quality and composure in possession
weaknesses: Limited appearances in 2024-25 (8 starts)
Not tested consistently against elite opposition

andy-robertson.name: Andy Robertson
andy-robertson.profile: Scotland's most decorated outfield player and a Champions League and Premier League winner with Liverpool. Robertson made 33 Premier League appearances in 2024-25, winning his second league title and playing a full role in one of the great Liverpool seasons. The vice-captain of the Scotland side, his energy, deliveries, and set-piece quality make him irreplaceable going into his first World Cup.
weaknesses: Defending in isolation against rapid wingers
Consistency in bigger games for Scotland

john-souttar.name: John Souttar
john-souttar.profile: A composed, tall centre-back who has flourished at Rangers since moving from Hearts. Souttar made 24 Premiership appearances in 2024-25, showing the reliability and aerial dominance that makes him a key defensive option for Scotland. His versatility to play both centre-back positions and his strong distribution fit Steve Clarke's system well.
weaknesses: History of significant knee injuries
Still building top-level European experience

kieran-tierney.name: Kieran Tierney
kieran-tierney.profile: One of the most naturally talented left-backs Scotland has produced, Tierney returned to boyhood club Celtic in June 2025 after his Arsenal contract expired. In his final Arsenal season (2024-25) he contributed 1 goal in his limited appearances having recovered from a hamstring injury sustained at Euro 2024. With the World Cup as motivation, Tierney's return to Celtic has revitalised him and he arrives in the best form of his career.
strengths: Attacking ability and carrying the ball
weaknesses: Recurring injury concerns throughout career
Limited Arsenal 2024-25 minutes due to hamstring injury

ryan-christie.name: Ryan Christie
ryan-christie.profile: A creative, hard-working attacking midfielder who was a regular in Bournemouth's Premier League survival campaigns. Christie made 27 starts and 42 substitute appearances across multiple seasons and scored 2 goals and contributed 3 assists in 2024-25 before a groin injury ended his season in April. His pressing, energy, and creative spark from wide midfield positions are important to Scotland's system.
weaknesses: Injury-disrupted end to 2024-25 season
Inconsistent final ball in big moments

findlay-curtis.name: Findlay Curtis
findlay-curtis.profile: A pacy, direct left winger who is one of the youngest and most exciting prospects in Scotland. Curtis made his Premiership debut for Rangers in February 2025 and then joined Kilmarnock on loan, scoring five goals in 14 games to help them avoid relegation. The 2026 World Cup represents a stunning breakthrough for the 20-year-old who embodies Scotland's generational renewal.
strengths: Directness and pace on the wing
weaknesses: Youth and inexperience at top level
Defensive contribution still developing

lewis-ferguson.name: Lewis Ferguson
lewis-ferguson.profile: A physically dominant, box-to-box midfielder who overcame a serious knee injury sustained in April 2024 to return for Bologna in November 2024. After his comeback he became a key figure, captaining Bologna to their first Coppa Italia title in 51 years. He brings incredible tenacity and midfield engine to Scotland's set-up as they head into their first World Cup since 1998.
weaknesses: Long-term knee injury — fitness question remains
Limited 2024-25 Serie A minutes due to injury comeback

ben-gannon-doak.name: Ben Gannon-Doak
ben-gannon-doak.profile: A thrilling young winger who spent 2024-25 on loan at Middlesbrough from Liverpool, earning the EFL Young Player of the Month award in November 2024 after five assists in five games. He scored 3 goals and recorded 7 assists in 24 Championship appearances before joining Bournemouth for £25m in August 2025. At 20, Doak is Scotland's brightest attacking talent and one of the most exciting players at the 2026 World Cup.
weaknesses: Youth and inconsistency at Premier League level
Still developing physically

jack-fletcher.name: Jack Fletcher
jack-fletcher.profile: A 18-year-old midfield prodigy born on 19 March 2007 and son of former Manchester United and Scotland midfielder Darren Fletcher. He was named in Manchester United's first-team matchday squad for the first time in October 2024 and made his senior debut in December 2025. Eligible for Scotland through his father, Fletcher's World Cup call-up at 18 represents extraordinary faith in an emerging talent.
strengths: Technical ability and ball control beyond his years
Potential to be a generational Scottish talent
weaknesses: Only 1 senior club appearance (debut December 2025)
Very limited top-level competitive experience

john-mcginn.name: John McGinn
john-mcginn.profile: Scotland's inspirational captain and the heartbeat of their midfield. McGinn scored his iconic solo run and finish against PSG in the Champions League quarter-final in April 2025, which was voted Aston Villa's Goal of the Season. He made 34 Premier League appearances in 2024-25, scoring 1 goal and providing 4 assists, while also winning 113 tackles across the season. He represents Scotland's first World Cup since 1998 as the emblem of this generation's achievement.
strengths: Goals and assists from midfield in big games
weaknesses: Occasional loss of composure in physical battles
Scotland's style heavily reliant on his energy levels

kenny-mclean.name: Kenny McLean
kenny-mclean.profile: A tough, ball-winning defensive midfielder who has been Norwich City's captain and linchpin for years. McLean made 33 Championship starts in 2024-25 and despite disciplinary issues — two suspensions and a chest infection — remained essential. His elite ball recovery rates and ability to screen the defence give Scotland defensive solidity in midfield at the World Cup.
weaknesses: Disciplinary record — multiple suspensions in 2024-25
Ageing profile at 33

scott-mctominay.name: Scott McTominay
scott-mctominay.profile: The star of Scotland's qualification campaign and one of the outstanding players in European football in 2024-25. McTominay joined Napoli for £25.7m in August 2024, scored 12 Serie A goals — the most of any midfielder in the league — and was named Serie A MVP as Napoli won the Scudetto. His Ballon d'Or nomination underlines how far he has come, and he will be Scotland's talisman as they make their first World Cup appearance since 1998.
strengths: Goals and goal threat from deep midfield
weaknesses: Can overcommit in defensive transitions at full throttle
Scotland rely heavily on his performances

che-adams.name: Che Adams
che-adams.profile: A tireless, dynamic striker who delivered his best-ever professional season in 2024-25, scoring 9 Serie A goals and providing 3 assists in 30 appearances for Torino. His long-range stunner against Empoli was one of the goals of the season in Italy. Born in England but choosing Scotland, Adams is the focal point of Steve Clarke's attack and has the physical and technical profile to trouble World Cup defenders.
strengths: Work rate and pressing from the front
Goals from long range and inside the box
Holds up play and brings teammates into the game
weaknesses: Shot conversion could be higher (22 shots on goal from 59)
Can drift out of games against deep, organised defences

lyndon-dykes.name: Lyndon Dykes
lyndon-dykes.profile: A robust, aerial target man who spent 2024-25 at Birmingham City, scoring goals and providing a physical focal point. Dykes joined Charlton Athletic in January 2026. Despite not being a prolific scorer in 2024-25, his aerial ability, hold-up play, and international experience make him a valuable squad option. His physical presence gives Scotland an alternative route to goal and is a test for any centre-back.
strengths: Aerial threat from crosses and set-pieces
Scotland's all-time leading scorer for goals per game ratio from a certain period
weaknesses: Touch and link-up play not at the highest level
Limited pace behind defenders

george-hirst.name: George Hirst
george-hirst.profile: A towering target man who made 33 appearances for newly promoted Ipswich Town in the Premier League in 2024-25, scoring 4 league goals despite the team's relegation battle. The son of former England international David Hirst, George has chosen Scotland and offers Steve Clarke a different physical dimension up front — a 6ft 3in presence who can win aerial duels and link play.
strengths: Link-up play for a big striker
Goals in his debut Premier League season
weaknesses: First-choice status for Scotland uncertain
Yet to establish himself as a reliable Premier League scorer

lawrence-shankland.name: Lawrence Shankland
lawrence-shankland.profile: Scotland's most prolific domestic striker who scored 24 league goals in both 2022-23 and 2023-24 before a quieter 2024-25 with 8 league goals for Hearts. Despite the dip, his clinical finishing, movement in the box, and quality from set-pieces make him Scotland's most reliable goal threat heading into their first World Cup since 1998. His transfer to Rangers was announced as Scotland prepared for the tournament.
strengths: Clinical finishing and movement in the box
Knowledge of scoring against Scottish Premiership-calibre opposition
weaknesses: Reduced output in 2024-25 compared to prior seasons
Unproven against top international defences

ross-stewart.name: Ross Stewart
ross-stewart.profile: A powerful, technically capable striker who made 12 Premier League appearances for relegated Southampton in 2024-25, scoring his first Premier League goal in the final game of the season against Arsenal. Stewart brings a complete forward's skillset — aerial presence, pace, and link-up play — and his first-hand experience of the Premier League hardship gives him a resilient mentality for World Cup football.
strengths: Pressing and workrate from the front
Composure on the ball for a big striker
weaknesses: Limited Premier League goals in 2024-25 (1 goal in 12 apps)
Southampton's relegation means top-flight preparation disrupted

mathew-ryan.name: Mathew Ryan
mathew-ryan.profile: Experienced goalkeeper from Australia with extensive European experience at top clubs. Known for shot-stopping ability and distribution skills.
weaknesses: Inconsistent club playing time at Levante
High-pressure match decision-making

paul-izzo.name: Paul Izzo
paul-izzo.profile: Reliable Danish Superliga goalkeeper competing for Australia. Physical presence with strong positioning in goal.
weaknesses: Distribution under pressure
Advanced age for international competition

patrick-beach.name: Patrick Beach
patrick-beach.profile: Young Australian goalkeeper competing in A-League. Key player for reigning A-League Champions Melbourne City with impressive form.
strengths: Young age with World Cup experience potential
weaknesses: Limited European experience
Occasional lapses in concentration

aziz-behich.name: Aziz Behich
aziz-behich.profile: Veteran left-back and Australian captain competing for fifth World Cup. Leader in defense with attacking contributions from fullback position.
weaknesses: Age-related decline in pace
Can be vulnerable to quick wingers

jordan-bos.name: Jordan Bos
jordan-bos.profile: Attack-minded left-back from Feyenoord competing at elite Dutch level. Athletic defender with strong ball progression skills.
weaknesses: Defensive positioning consistency
Experience in major tournaments

cameron-burgess.name: Cameron Burgess
cameron-burgess.profile: Experienced center-back competing in English Championship. Dominant aerial presence and physical defender with leadership qualities.
weaknesses: Pace against agile attackers
Ball-playing ability in possession

alessandro-circati.name: Alessandro Circati
alessandro-circati.profile: Young center-back on loan at Parma from Serie A club. Developing defender with good technical ability and positional awareness.
weaknesses: Limited Serie A experience
Physical development against physical strikers

milo-degenek.name: Miloš Degenek
milo-degenek.profile: Veteran defender competing in Cypriot football. Experienced center-back bringing leadership and tactical intelligence to backline.
weaknesses: Declining pace
Recovery speed against quick attackers

jason-geria.name: Jason Geria
jason-geria.profile: Veteran right-back competing in Japanese J-League. Experienced fullback with consistent defensive contributions.
weaknesses: Limited attacking contribution
Age-related physicality concerns

lucas-herrington.name: Lucas Herrington
lucas-herrington.profile: Young fullback making impact in MLS with Colorado Rapids. Promising defender with athleticism and potential for development.
weaknesses: Inexperience at international level
Tactical maturity and consistency

jacob-italiano.name: Jacob Italiano
jacob-italiano.profile: Midfielder-turned-defender at Austrian Bundesliga club. Versatile player capable of defensive contributions from midfield or backline.
weaknesses: Defensive positioning consistency
Limited left-side coverage

harry-souttar.name: Harry Souttar
harry-souttar.profile: Scottish-Australian center-back at Leicester City. Tall, physically dominant defender with aerial prowess.
weaknesses: Limited playing time at Leicester
Pace against quick attackers

kai-trewin.name: Kai Trewin
kai-trewin.profile: Right-back competing in MLS for NYCFC. Solid defender with reliability and consistent performances.
weaknesses: Limited attacking contribution
Pace against elite wingers

cameron-devlin.name: Cameron Devlin
cameron-devlin.profile: Defensive midfielder at Hearts competing in Scottish Premiership. Ball-winning midfielder with strong pressing and recovery skills.
weaknesses: Passing accuracy under pressure
Limited creative output

ajdin-hrusti.name: Ajdin Hrustić
ajdin-hrusti.profile: Creative midfielder at Dutch Eredivisie side. Playmaking midfielder with assist potential and technical ability.
weaknesses: Defensive contribution
Physical presence in midfield

jackson-irvine.name: Jackson Irvine
jackson-irvine.profile: Veteran box-to-box midfielder at 2. Bundesliga side. Leader in midfield with strong physical presence and work rate.
weaknesses: Recovering from injury
Age-related decline in athleticism

connor-metcalfe.name: Connor Metcalfe
connor-metcalfe.profile: Attacking midfielder competing in 2. Bundesliga with St. Pauli. Technical midfielder with creative contributions.
weaknesses: Physical presence in midfield
Defensive contribution consistency

aiden-o-neill.name: Aiden O'Neill
aiden-o-neill.profile: Midfielder competing in MLS for NYCFC. Versatile midfielder capable of playing multiple positions.
weaknesses: Limited goal contribution
Consistency in performances

paul-okon-engstler.name: Paul Okon-Engstler
paul-okon-engstler.profile: Young midfielder for A-League side Sydney FC. Developing player with strong ball-winning and defensive capabilities.
weaknesses: Experience at international level
Technical consistency

nestory-irankunda.name: Nestory Irankunda
nestory-irankunda.profile: Young winger from Bayern Munich's academy signed by Watford. Pacey left-winger with dribbling skills and potential.
strengths: Young age with World Cup potential
weaknesses: Decision-making in final third
Consistency in performances

mathew-leckie.name: Mathew Leckie
mathew-leckie.profile: Veteran winger and 2026 World Cup veteran. Experienced wide forward with leadership qualities in attacking play.
weaknesses: Age-related decline in pace
Inconsistency in recent seasons

awer-mabil.name: Awer Mabil
awer-mabil.profile: Winger at Spanish Segunda División club. Experienced forward with goal and assist contributions.
weaknesses: Physical intensity waning with age
Consistency in conversion

mohamed-toure.name: Mohamed Touré
mohamed-toure.profile: Young striker breaking through at Norwich City in Championship. Clinical finisher with early season impact.
weaknesses: Limited experience in major leagues
Consistency at higher level unproven

nishan-velupillay.name: Nishan Velupillay
nishan-velupillay.profile: Attacking midfielder/winger for A-League side Melbourne Victory. Dynamic forward with goal-scoring run in recent form.
weaknesses: Defensive tracking
Consistency across seasons

cristian-volpato.name: Cristian Volpato
cristian-volpato.profile: Young attacking midfielder at Italian Serie B side Sassuolo. Technical forward with creative and goal-scoring capability.
weaknesses: Inconsistency in Serie B
Physical development against stronger opponents

tete-yengi.name: Tete Yengi
tete-yengi.profile: Forward competing in Scottish Premiership with Livingston. Attack-minded forward with goal-scoring contributions.
weaknesses: Limited playing time in Premiership
Consistency in conversions

orlando-gill.name: Orlando Gill
orlando-gill.profile: Reliable goalkeeper with solid positioning and distribution skills. Backup option in the Paraguay national team.
strengths: Communication and leadership on set pieces
weaknesses: Limited reflexes for high-pressure situations
Occasional decision-making errors in one-on-ones

roberto-fernandez.name: Roberto Fernández
roberto-fernandez.profile: Experienced domestic goalkeeper competing in Paraguay's top division. Provides depth to the goalkeeping contingent.
weaknesses: Limited experience at elite level
Ball-playing abilities require development

gaston-olveira.name: Gastón Olveira
gaston-olveira.profile: Domestic-based goalkeeper with consistent performances in Paraguay's top division. Third-choice keeper for the national team.
strengths: Familiarity with South American football style
weaknesses: Limited high-level competition exposure
Distribution from the back needs improvement

juan-caceres.name: Juan Cáceres
juan-caceres.profile: Pacey right-back competing in the Russian Premier League. Offers attacking thrust down the flank with defensive discipline.
strengths: Pace and acceleration in open play
weaknesses: Concentration lapses in tight defensive situations
Set-piece defending consistency

gustavo-velazquez.name: Gustavo Velázquez
gustavo-velazquez.profile: Experienced center-back leading Paraguay's defense from the domestic league. Commanding presence with tactical intelligence.
weaknesses: Limited pace against quicker forwards
Ball-playing ability at elite level

gustavo-gomez.name: Gustavo Gómez
gustavo-gomez.profile: Dominant center-back at Brazilian powerhouse Palmeiras. Captain-like figure providing experience and aerial dominance for Paraguay.
weaknesses: Occasional lapses in concentration
Limited pace for pressing opposition

junior-alonso.name: Júnior Alonso
junior-alonso.profile: Veteran center-back with Atlético Mineiro bringing experience and leadership. Solid defender focused on positioning over athleticism.
weaknesses: Declining pace with age
Struggle against pacey, direct forwards

jose-canale.name: José Cañale
jose-canale.profile: Young, energetic left-back at Argentine club Lanús. Offers pace and athleticism down the left flank with improving defensive awareness.
weaknesses: Inconsistent defensive positioning
